question: to the Commission Anja Hazekamp (The Left) Subject:

Research by Politico reveals that the International Fur Federation has funded its European policy work through a Liechtenstein trust fund that also received money from Russian auctions1. The 2023 financial statements of the lobbying organisation show that EUR 223 870 came from the Russian fur auction house Sojuzpushnina, based in St. Petersburg, of which EUR 216 000 was allegedly used to pay the lobbyist of the International Fur Federation in Brussels. In 2025, the European Commissioner for Animal Welfare held another lobbying meeting with the International Fur Federation and Fur Europe, the lobbying organisation into which the Federation has since merged, to discuss the European Citizens’ Initiative ‘Fur Free Europe’2. 1.

Can the Commission confirm that the revenues received by the International Fur Federation from the Russian fur auction house are covered by EU sanctions and are therefore in violation of EU sanctions against Russia?
Does the Commission agree that lobbying organisations receiving Russian revenues should not be able to influence EU policies?

When will the Commission introduce a European ban on keeping and killing animals for fur production and on importing fur, as requested by more than 1.5 million EU citizens in the European Citizens’ Initiative ‘Fur Free Europe’3?

answer: (English version) to the Commission Anja Hazekamp (The Left) (2 July 2026) Subject: Influence of Russian fur revenue on European policymaking Research by Politico reveals that the International Fur Federation has funded its European policy work through a Liechtenstein trust fund that also received money from Russian auctions (1). The 2023 financial statements of the lobbying organisation show that EUR 223 870 came from the Russian fur auction house Sojuzpushnina, based in St. Petersburg, of which EUR 216 000 was allegedly used to pay the lobbyist of the International Fur Federation in Brussels. In 2025, the European Commissioner for Animal Welfare held another lobbying meeting with the International Fur Federation and Fur Europe, the lobbying organisation into which the Federation has since merged, to discuss the European Citizens’ Initiative ‘Fur Free Europe’ (2). 1. Can the Commission confirm that the revenues received by the International Fur Federation from the Russian fur auction house are covered by EU sanctions and are therefore in violation of EU sanctions against Russia? 2. Does the Commission agree that lobbying organisations receiving Russian revenues should not be able to influence EU policies? 3. When will the Commission introduce a European ban on keeping and killing animals for fur production and on importing fur, as requested by more than 1.5 million EU citizens in the European Citizens’ Initiative ‘Fur Free Europe’ (3)? (21 August 2026) The enforcement of EU sanctions is primarily the responsibility of the Member States’ competent authorities, which assess possible breaches on a case-by-case basis. Any indication of a breach should be examined by the relevant national authorities. Council Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 of 31 July 2014 concerning restrictive measures in view of Russia's actions destabilising the situation in Ukraine (1), Article 5n, prohibits EU-based firms from providing a range of services. This includes public relations services (lobbying) for the Government of Russia or any legal person, entity or body established in Russia. This may affect registrants of the Transparency Register. It should also be noted that the Commission applies strict rules on stakeholder contacts in EU decision-making and policy implementation: Commissioners, Cabinet members and managers may meet only registered interest representatives and information and minutes of those meetings are published under Commission Decisions (EU) 2024/3081 (2) and 2024/3082 (3). The International Fur Federation is registered in the Transparency Register (TR REG number 311679992366-03 (4)) and appears to have removed their Russian member from their website. As a registrant, this entity is bound by the code of conduct for registrants under the applicable interinstitutional agreement (5). The preparations for the follow-up Commission Communication replying to the European Citizens’ Initiative ‘Fur Free Europe’ are ongoing.
